back: Direct materials consumed + direct labour + direct expenses.
Indirect factory costs that cannot be traced to each unit: factory rent, power, indirect wages, depreciation of factory machinery.
Goods started but not finished at a date; a current asset at the year end.
Opening raw materials + purchases + carriage inwards − returns − closing raw materials.
Prime cost + factory overheads + opening work in progress − closing work in progress.
Royalties or licence fees paid per unit made; hire of a special machine for one product.
Wages of supervisors, storekeepers, cleaners and maintenance staff: a factory overhead, not direct labour.

front: Where do office and selling costs go in a manufacturer?
back: Income statement expenses, never the manufacturing account.

front: Why adjust work in progress after overheads?
back: Half-finished goods have used overheads as well as direct costs, so they are valued at full factory cost.
